# Code of conduct

## The short version

Be decent to people. Argue with the work, not the person who did it.

<br>

## What this repository particularly needs

This is a course, so the people in its issues are frequently saying **I did not understand this**. That takes more nerve than filing a bug, and a repository that makes it embarrassing gets no such reports and quietly stops improving.

So:

- **A reader who is lost has found a defect.** [`something-is-unclear`](ISSUE_TEMPLATE/something-is-unclear.yml) is a bug report, and it will be treated as one. Nobody will be told to read more carefully.
- **No level of prior knowledge is assumed or required.** The course claims no prerequisites and that claim is tested by beginners reporting where it fails.
- **Correcting the material is welcome and correcting a person is not the same thing.** "This number is wrong, here is what I measured" is the best issue anybody can open. "You clearly do not understand X" is not, even when it happens to be true.

<br>

## Not acceptable

Harassment, insults, or personal attacks. Sexualised language or imagery. Demeaning comments about anyone's background, identity or level of experience. Publishing anyone's private information. Sustained disruption of discussions.

That applies in issues, pull requests, discussions, commit messages and code review on this repository.

<br>

## Reporting

Email **ameythakur20@gmail.com** with `AI-ENGINEERING` in the subject. Reports go to one person, are not shared further, and are read.

There is no committee here, so the honest description of enforcement is that the maintainer will edit or delete comments, close threads, and block accounts as needed, and will say when he has done so.

<br>

## Scope

This applies to everyone taking part, including the maintainer. If the maintainer is dismissive of a beginner's question, that is a breach of this document and worth saying so.
